cases.title: Tidy labels says which pipe's label would move and by how many millimetres, and Esc moves nothing
cases.plan_item: Tidy labels names the pipe (gap plan section 3 item 7; BUG-856; regression C37; run 47 B.4.2)
cases.reviewed_against: builder-filled: Opus review still needed. Compared by the builder on 24 Oct 2026 with card C37 (TEST_CASES_DRAFT_22OCT.md) and robot run 47 B.4.2: the P8 line with 275 mm, Will move 1, Esc gives Nothing was moved, one cancelled outcome line. The card's no-clear-spot summary count is recorded, not asserted.
cases.expected: With the switch on and the SPOT LEVEL block 10EC5D moved next to the new pit, CDTIDYLABELS with the answer All prints '[CE] Will move 1', then the line 'pipe P8 -> open end start invert text would move 275 mm (further out).' so the drafter can see WHICH pipe's label is affected and by how much; it asks 'Move this label now? [Yes/No] <No>:' and one Esc prints '[CE] Nothing was moved.'; the Civil log holds one 'Command outcome: CDTIDYLABELS cancelled'; the drawing holds the same number of objects afterwards.
cases.why_not_unit: The preview words come from the real labels, pipes and pits in the drawing and the live label-placement search; only the live command line shows them.
not_automated: Apply with Yes and the U/REDO of the applied move (Codex W4-01 to W4-05) are not driven here.
The handle 10EC5D is a fixture handle read from the master drawing; the case records what it is (name and layer) but does not check that it is a SPOT LEVEL block (run 47 used it as the obstruction).
The 'No clear spot found: pipe P3 -> P2' line of the same preview is recorded, not asserted.
